lens: Archival historian — assessing whether the rubric weights primary sources the way the discipline does, whether it handles the argument from silence correctly (differential survival of records, classification as a non-random filter on evidence), whether it distinguishes evidence for a proposition from evidence about a place, and whether it can express the three separate propositions every site carries: that it exists, what it was for, and what it is now.
verdict: NEEDS RESTRUCTURING — not fixable by reweighting. The six axes and the composite formula are a sound *intelligence-fusion* instrument bolted to *historical* grade labels, and the two disagree. Six specific defects are fatal and each is demonstrable by arithmetic on a real facility: (1) evidence has no polarity, so a primary document proving a claim was fabricated adds to DOC; (2) the grade attaches to a place while evidence attaches to propositions, so every real base becomes a credibility donor to whatever is claimed about it; (3) CONFIDENCE-in-evidence is published under labels that assert EXISTENCE, with no expected-record prior, so the Greenbrier in 1991 scores E ("folklore with a trace") while fully operational; (4) GEO at .22 encodes a buried-rural-mountain prior that structurally caps every urban, above-ground, or in-building hardened facility below A no matter how well documented; (5) there is no diagnosticity term, so a commercial limestone warehouse (SubTropolis) scores C as a hardened-facility candidate purely for having an adit, a substation, and a rail spur; (6) a single conclusive primary document with nothing else attached tops out at 28.0 → E, which inverts the foundational premise of documentary history. The scoring core needs to be rebuilt around propositions rather than sites, with signed evidence, likelihood ratios rather than presence counts, and an explicit separation of P(exists) from Q(evidence). The provenance tiers, the CONTAM concept, the lineage-tracing commitment, and the retain-the-negatives rule are all good and should survive the rebuild.

failures.problem: Evidence has no sign. Every axis counts evidence *presence*; nothing in the formula can encode evidence that a claim is FALSE. Disconfirmation can only be expressed by declining to award points, which is indistinguishable from having looked and found nothing. REFUTER exists in the fleet but has no numeric hook into CONFIDENCE, so 'refuted' becomes a flag that sits beside a passing grade rather than a force that drives the score down.
failures.worked_example: Dulce Base, NM. The single strongest piece of evidence in the case is a primary-grade record of the FABRICATION: the AFOSI counterintelligence operation run against Paul Bennewitz c.1979-1982, in which Richard C. Doty fed Bennewitz forged documents and staged material to steer him away from classified Kirtland AFB programs — established by Doty's own on-record admissions and by named investigative work (Greg Bishop, 'Project Beta'). Under §1.1 as written, 'declassified records' and 'investigative journalism with named sourcing' earn DOC points. An ASSESSOR following the axis text literally credits the disinformation documentation to DOC — the proof of manufacture raises the candidate's score. Separately, SubTropolis (Kansas City) is affirmatively, provably a commercial warehouse cave, and the rubric produces 67.45 → C for it; the REFUTER's refutation cannot move that number, so the register publishes a C-grade row flagged 'refuted', which contradicts itself on its own face.
failures.proposed_fix: Make evidence signed. Each source carries a direction (+supports / −undercuts) and a magnitude against a named proposition. Add a REFUTATION channel that can drive the composite to a floor independent of the additive axes, and add a grade band below F — R (REFUTED: affirmatively shown mundane or fabricated, with the refuting source cited) — distinct from F (no evidence either way). F and R are epistemically opposite states and the current scale collapses them.

failures.problem: The unit of grading is a PLACE; the unit of evidence is a PROPOSITION. Because DOC/GEO/INF/OWN accrue to the site, a well-documented real installation launders its documentation onto every claim ever attached to it. This is precisely the citogenesis mechanism §1.3 exists to fight, executed by the register itself.
failures.worked_example: Camp Hero / Montauk Air Force Station, NY. The base is thoroughly real: Army coastal artillery from 1942, USAF radar station 1952-1981, the AN/FPS-35 tower still standing, NARA unit records, BRAC/disposal records, EPA files, NY State Parks acquisition. Scored as a site: DOC 92, GEO 90, INF 78, OWN 92, TEST 70, COR 85, CONTAM 5 → 84.42 → B. Now score the 'Montauk Project' claim — vast underground levels, time and mind-control experiments — which originates entirely with Preston Nichols' recovered memories in the 1992 book co-authored with Peter Moon. The axes are unchanged because they describe the site; only CONTAM moves to 100 → 43.29 → D, 'weak inference, suggestive but thin.' A recovered-memory claim from one 1992 book is rendered as 'suggestive' solely because it is pinned to a real radar station. The rubric never says which of these two numbers the register publishes, because it has no concept that they are two different candidates.
failures.proposed_fix: Grade CLAIMS, not sites. A site record becomes a container holding N independently graded propositions (exists / had function X / has current status Y / has feature Z), each with its own axis scores, CONTAM, and grade. The site's headline grade is the EXISTENCE proposition only; every other assertion on the page renders its own badge. This also fixes Mount Weather, where the facility is A-grade but the most-repeated content about it — the 'underground city' with streets, sidewalks, a small lake, and its own transit system — traces to one article, Richard Pollock, 'The Mysterious Mountain,' The Progressive, March 1976, sourced to unnamed off-the-record former officials. That is P3 publication resting on P5 testimony: the exact citogenesis pattern §1.3 defines, currently with nowhere to attach except an entry the interface will render green.

failures.problem: Confidence in EVIDENCE is published under labels that assert EXISTENCE, and there is no expected-record prior. The historian's argument from silence is only valid where the silence is surprising. For a classified facility, absent records are the expected condition and carry near-zero negative information — but the rubric treats a documentary void identically whether the record class never existed, was destroyed, or was searched and found empty.
failures.worked_example: The Greenbrier / Project Greek Island, scored as of 1991. Built 1958-61, 1,100 beds, fully staffed, the designated relocation site for the entire United States Congress, concealed behind Forsythe Associates as a resort TV contractor. Best-faith 1991 scores: DOC 5 (nothing declassified, appropriations buried), GEO 40, INF 55, OWN 35, TEST 45 (persistent, specific local worker lore), COR 30, CONTAM 55 → 22.91 → E, 'Folklore with a trace. Claim has an identifiable origin and nothing more.' The register would have published the most important congressional COG facility in the country as folklore. On 31 May 1992 Ted Gup published in the Washington Post and the same facility recomputes to 90.46 → A, with zero change to any physical fact. The rubric measured disclosure and printed it as reality.
failures.proposed_fix: Split the output into two published numbers: Q(EVIDENCE) — what the current axes measure, honestly labeled as quality-of-record — and P(EXISTS) — a separate estimate. Introduce an EXPECTED-RECORD prior per era/typology/agency: how likely is it that a facility of this class, in this period, would have a surviving public record at all? Where that prior is low, a DOC of 5 is uninformative and must not be allowed to drag P(EXISTS). Rewrite the grade band prose so it describes evidence states, not existence states ('A = documentarily established' vs 'E = single traceable origin, no corroboration'), and never let an evidence grade wear existence language.

failures.problem: GEO's .22 weight encodes a buried-rural-mountain prior into the arithmetic. Every GEO criterion — tunnel/adit symbols, spoil, cut-and-cover scarring, blast-portal morphology, anomalous road grade into terrain, terrain suitability, rock competence, water table — is null for urban, in-building, or above-ground hardened facilities. Those sites cannot reach A by construction, regardless of documentation.
failures.worked_example: 33 Thomas Street, Manhattan (AT&T Long Lines Building / NSA TITANPOINTE). Windowless brutalist tower, Warnecke, 1969-74, purpose-built hardened, houses a major international gateway switch. Documentation is overwhelming and primary: NYC Department of Buildings filings, AT&T's own engineering and route literature, FCC records, the architect's papers, and the Snowden material published by The Intercept in November 2016. Scores: DOC 88, GEO 20 (no adit, no spoil, no terrain, no restricted airspace — the axis's criteria are simply inapplicable), INF 98, OWN 92, TEST 70, COR 88, CONTAM 5 → 72.11 → B. Even with a charitable GEO 40 it only reaches 76.40 → B. To clear A=85 it would need GEO≈71, which this axis's own criteria cannot generate for a Manhattan building. The same defect hits PEF Cartwheel at Fort Reno Park, Washington DC — a documented Presidential Emergency Facility on the microwave network with a direct AT&T cable route to the White House — which scores DOC 75, GEO 25, INF 85, OWN 70, TEST 45, COR 55, CONTAM 25 → 53.11 → D, 'weak inference,' for a facility whose existence and function appear in Army Signal Agency and WHCA records.
failures.proposed_fix: Make weights typology-conditional, and make axes droppable. If an axis is inapplicable to a typology, drop it and renormalize the remaining weights rather than scoring it zero. Define per-typology profiles (buried-rural, urban-hardened, in-building, silo, relay/comms, archive) each with its own weight vector and its own GEO criteria — a Manhattan facility's geospatial signature is setback, structural loading, vent stack morphology, and floor-plate depth, not spoil piles.

failures.problem: No diagnosticity term. The axes reward the PRESENCE of signals, not the power of those signals to discriminate the hardened-facility hypothesis from the mundane one. Signals that are near-certain under 'it is a big industrial site' have a likelihood ratio near 1 and should contribute nothing, but the rubric awards them full value.
failures.worked_example: SubTropolis, Kansas City — an operating commercial underground business park in a former limestone mine, with no defense function whatsoever. Honest scores against the axis text: DOC 65 (MSHA permits and Missouri DNR filings are P1 'filed permits'), GEO 88 (adits, portals, spoil, anomalous road grade into the bluff — textbook morphology on quads and imagery), INF 70 (dedicated substation, an actual rail spur, deep wells, generator and fuel permits — every INF criterion literally satisfied), OWN 78, TEST 20, COR 65, CONTAM 5 → 67.45 → C, 'Reasonable inference. Converging open signals.' A warehouse cave grades as a reasonable hardened-facility inference because a limestone mine necessarily has holes, power, water, and rail. The register will fill with C-grade quarries.
failures.proposed_fix: Replace additive presence-scoring with likelihood ratios against an explicit null hypothesis. Each signal is scored as P(signal | hardened) / P(signal | mundane alternative), and the mundane alternative must be NAMED per candidate ('this is a commercial limestone mine', 'this is a municipal water tank', 'this is a cell tower compound'). REFUTER's job becomes proposing the null; signals that the null explains equally well score ~0. Require every candidate above D to have a named-and-rejected mundane alternative on the record.

failures.problem: A single conclusive primary source cannot exceed grade E. Because DOC is capped at weight .28, DOC=100 with all other axes at zero yields exactly 28.00. The grade band PROSE describes evidence KINDS ('A = Primary sources establish existence and function') while the FORMULA measures evidence BREADTH across six modalities. These are different instruments and they disagree by up to three grade bands on the same candidate.
failures.worked_example: Compute it directly: DOC 100, GEO 0, INF 0, OWN 0, TEST 0, COR 0, CONTAM 0 → 28.00 → E, 'Folklore with a trace.' This is not hypothetical. A demolished 1950s AT&T Long Lines hardened underground repeater station, documented by its FCC filings and AT&T's own published route records and by nothing else, satisfies the prose definition of A exactly — primary sources establish existence and function — and computes to C or below. The Deep Underground Command Center is the sharpest case (below). Six-modality convergence is an intelligence-fusion standard; documentary history holds that one unambiguous primary source can settle a fact, and this formula cannot express that.
failures.proposed_fix: Add a documentary sufficiency override: a P1 source that names the facility, its location, and its function, and is judged authentic, sets a grade FLOOR of B for the existence proposition regardless of the other axes. Convergence should raise confidence above that floor; its absence must not pull below it. Alternatively make the composite a max-of-paths rather than a weighted mean, so any single sufficient path to knowledge can carry the entry.

failures.problem: COR and CONTAM are the same variable measured twice — once additively, once multiplicatively — and their combined swing exceeds the entire DOC axis. Source independence is therefore weighted more heavily than documentary primacy, inverting the discipline's ordering.
failures.worked_example: Arithmetic: COR contributes .10 × [0..100] = 10 points of swing. CONTAM multiplies by [1.0 .. 0.5], which on a typical base of 60-70 is another 30-35 points. Combined swing from one conceptual variable — 'how many independent lineages are there' — is ~40-45 points, or two-plus grade bands. DOC's total swing across its full range is 28 points. A candidate with many mutually-independent secondary lineages therefore outranks a candidate with a single archival original. Watch it move Dulce Base: CONTAM 95 → 17.01 → F, but §1.3's own calibration text says '50 = two or three independent origins with heavy downstream copying,' and Dulce genuinely has three nominally distinct named claimants (Bennewitz 1979-80, 'Thomas Castello' and the Dulce Papers c.1987, Phil Schneider 1990s). A scorer following §1.3 literally sets CONTAM ~55 → 23.49 → E. The rubric's own calibration text contradicts the answer the rubric needs.
failures.proposed_fix: Collapse COR and CONTAM into one independence term applied once. Rewrite the CONTAM calibration so origins must be CAUSALLY independent, not merely distinct persons: a chain of claimants inside one subculture who read each other is ONE lineage, however many names it has. Add an explicit test — 'would this source have produced this claim if the prior source had never existed?'

failures.problem: CONTAM cannot distinguish one lineage of RUMOR from one lineage of SCHOLARSHIP. It counts intermediaries, not underlying witnesses. A single diligent compiler who cites forty primary documents is penalized identically to a single anonymous forum post.
failures.worked_example: PEF Cartwheel and the other Presidential Emergency Facilities (Cannonball at Cross Mountain PA, Cowpuncher at Martinsburg WV, Corkscrew at Lambs Knoll). Essentially the entire public web presence of these sites descends from two compilation efforts — coldwar-c4i.net and the WHCA history blog — which themselves assemble White House Army Signal Agency and AT&T primary records. LINEAGE correctly reports one downstream lineage and CONTAM lands at 25-60, applying a 12-30% multiplicative penalty to a candidate whose underlying evidence is a stack of P1 documents. That penalty is what drags Cartwheel from a 60.70 base to 53.11 → D. A critical edition is one lineage; its witnesses are many, and no historian would penalize the facts for having been collated well.
failures.proposed_fix: Compute CONTAM on the graph of ORIGINAL WITNESSES, not on the graph of publications. If a single compiler cites forty independent primary documents, CONTAM is low and the compiler is a transparent intermediary. Add an intermediary-transparency test: does the secondary source expose its primaries such that they can be independently pulled? If yes, it passes through; if it cannot be checked, it is a lineage terminus.

failures.problem: The firewall covers DOC only. GEO, INF, OWN, TEST and COR have no provenance gating at all, so a claim with zero documentary standing can still accumulate 72 points of headroom across the ungated axes. TEST is the worst: its criterion is 'named worker accounts,' which a pseudonymous fabrication satisfies verbatim.
failures.worked_example: Dulce Base again. DOC is correctly firewalled at 40. But GEO scores off P2 imagery of a real mesa with real terrain and real access roads, INF off real regional substations and gas infrastructure, and TEST off 'Thomas Castello' — a named worker account, which is exactly what the TEST axis asks for and which is almost certainly an invented persona. Those ungated axes contribute 21.2 points before CONTAM. More generally: any P5 claimant who points at a hillside gets GEO scored from P2 imagery, because the IMAGERY is primary-derived even though the CLAIM that the imagery is relevant is P5. The tier of a source and the tier of the inference drawn from it are being confused.
failures.proposed_fix: Extend the firewall to every axis with per-axis caps keyed to the best supporting tier. TEST specifically needs identity verification as a gate: an account counts as named only if the person is independently confirmed to exist and to have been in a position to know. Score the INFERENCE's tier, not the artifact's — imagery is P2, but 'this imagery shows a portal' is an interpretation and inherits the tier of whoever asserted it.

failures.problem: Evidence for a PROGRAM is credited at full strength to every candidate INSTANCE. There is no mechanism to divide evidentiary weight across a candidate set, so one appropriations line or one executive order can be cited at full value by ten different candidate sites, inflating DOC across the whole register.
failures.worked_example: The Presidential Emergency Facility program is documented at program level — WHCA and Army Signal Agency records establish that roughly eight PEFs existed on the microwave net around Washington. That document is evidence that any GIVEN unidentified hilltop is a PEF only in proportion to 8 divided by the number of candidate hilltops. Under the rubric it is a P1 'declassified record' and every candidate that cites it takes full DOC credit. Ten candidates each score DOC 75 off one document that supports eight facilities, several of them not on the candidate list. The same applies to the Federal Relocation Arc: the program is documented, the individual site identities were withheld, and the rubric will happily let program documentation certify wrong pins.
failures.proposed_fix: Tag every source with its SCOPE — class-level or instance-level — and gate the DOC contribution accordingly. Class-level evidence establishes that the typology exists in the region and contributes to a PRIOR, not to the instance's DOC. Only evidence that identifies THIS site (coordinates, parcel, named installation, matched photograph) contributes instance DOC. Enforce it at write time: a source cited by more than one candidate must be marked class-level or the entity resolution is wrong.

failures.problem: No status band for proposed / studied / cancelled / never-built, and the Status taxonomy's nearest option is 'alleged-only,' which is epistemically opposite. Well-documented non-facilities land in the folklore bin next to inventions.
failures.worked_example: The Deep Underground Command Center (DUCC) — proposed 1962-64, a 3,000-4,000 ft command post near the Pentagon, 'Austere' (50 person) and 'Moderate' (300 person) variants, approved by McNamara and Rusk, reached the President, killed when Congress declined FY1965 funds and the committee chairmen refused reprogramming for feasibility studies. Documentation is superb and primary: JCS memoranda published in Foreign Relations of the United States 1964-68 vol. X, declassified feasibility studies, the Hitch memorandum. Score: DOC 90, GEO 0 (nothing was ever dug), INF 10, OWN 20, TEST 30, COR 70, CONTAM 10 → 37.24 → E, 'Folklore with a trace. Claim has an identifiable origin and nothing more.' DUCC is the opposite of folklore — it is a proven non-facility, one of the best-documented COG proposals in the American record — and it scores six points above Dulce Base. The register will either omit it, losing exactly the material it should hold, or publish it beside inventions.
failures.proposed_fix: Add PROPOSED / STUDIED / CANCELLED / NEVER-BUILT to the Status axis, and let a candidate be graded A on the proposition 'this program was proposed and cancelled' while being R on 'this facility exists.' This falls straight out of the claims-not-sites restructuring: existence and program-history are separate propositions with separate grades.

failures.problem: Location precision is a filter, not a score input, so nothing couples evidence quality to coordinate quality. A high-grade candidate with a guessed coordinate renders on the map as a pin identical to a surveyed one — the register performing its own citogenesis at the interface layer.
failures.worked_example: Any Federal Relocation Arc site documented at program level with 'claimed-only' location precision. DOC scores off the program record, the composite clears C or B, and MapLibre draws a dot. Six months later that dot is the most-cited coordinate for the site on the open web, because it is the only structured, machine-readable, apparently-authoritative one. The register will have manufactured a precise fact out of an imprecise one — the identical mechanism to the Mount Weather 'underground lake', which is one 1976 Progressive article repeated until it reads as established. §1.4's stated purpose is to stop claims recirculating; this pathway starts new ones.
failures.proposed_fix: Make location precision a hard gate on rendering, not a filter: anything below 'approximate' renders as a region polygon or a county centroid with visible uncertainty, never a point. Grade the LOCATION proposition separately from the EXISTENCE proposition and display both badges on the map popup. A candidate can legitimately be A on existence and F on location, and the map must show that.

failures.problem: Differential survival of records is treated as if it were evidence about the facility. The rubric has no term for 'the record class that would have carried this evidence no longer exists,' and two of its named source types are inversely correlated with the property being detected.
failures.worked_example: Two concrete mechanisms. First, the NPRC fire: on 12 July 1973 the National Personnel Records Center in St. Louis burned for 22 hours, destroying 16-18 million Official Military Personnel Files — roughly 80% of Army discharges 1912-1960 and 75% of Air Force discharges 1947-1964 — with no duplicates, no microfilm, and no index. TEST explicitly rewards 'unit histories, service records, obituaries citing assignments.' Every early-Cold-War Army or Air Force facility therefore has a structurally suppressed TEST axis for a reason having nothing to do with the facility, and the rubric reads that suppression as weak evidence. Second, NEPA/EIS filings and FCC antenna registrations are named as DOC and INF earners, but classified actions receive classified annexes or categorical exclusions and genuinely covert emitters do not register — so availability of those records ANTI-correlates with sensitivity. The rubric measures how visible a facility is and prints the answer under a heading about how real it is.
failures.proposed_fix: Add a per-axis APPLICABILITY/SURVIVAL flag: 'searched, found nothing' vs 'record class destroyed' vs 'record class never existed for this category' vs 'not yet searched.' Only the first is negative evidence; the rest must renormalize the axis out rather than score it zero. Publish the known-bias statement on the methodology page — the sampling frame is biased toward the disclosed, and a register that does not say so is misrepresenting its own coverage.

failures.problem: Versioned grades render disclosure history as evidence history, with no annotation distinguishing the two. Combined with REFUTER's stated 'defaults to refuted under uncertainty,' the register systematically under-registers the contemporary, still-classified facilities that are its entire reason for existing.
failures.worked_example: Greenbrier moves E (22.91) → A (90.46) across 31 May 1992 with no physical change; the confidence-history graph will show a vertical line that a reader parses as 'the evidence got better,' when what happened is one reporter published. Run it in reverse: Mount Weather's current post-2001 function is far less documented than its 1970s function was after the Pollock article, so its function grade DROPS over time while the facility becomes more operationally central. A falling line on a confidence chart is visually indistinguishable from 'we now think this is less real.' Meanwhile REFUTER's refute-by-default prior is a strong bias against existence applied to precisely the domain where non-disclosure is the norm, not the exception.
failures.proposed_fix: Annotate every grade transition with its CAUSE from a controlled vocabulary — new-disclosure / new-search / re-analysis / refutation / status-change — and render disclosure-driven moves in a visually distinct style from evidence-driven ones. Replace REFUTER's blanket refute-by-default with a typology-conditional prior: default-refute for high-base-rate mundane categories (mines, water infrastructure, telecom huts), default-open for categories where the base rate of concealment is known to be high.

calibration_set.name: Cheyenne Mountain Complex, CO — existence and original function
calibration_set.reasoning: POSITIVE CONTROL, high end. Publicly acknowledged since construction, exhaustive primary documentation (Army Corps engineering records, DTIC reports, congressional appropriations, GAO reviews), exact surveyed location, published photography, named personnel by the thousand, many fully independent lineages. Rubric computes 94.26 → A. The rubric gets this RIGHT and should continue to.

calibration_set.name: Cheyenne Mountain Complex — the claim 'it is the current NORAD headquarters'
calibration_set.reasoning: NEGATIVE CONTROL on STATUS, same site as above. NORAD/USNORTHCOM operations consolidated at Peterson AFB in 2006 and the complex went to alternate/warm-standby status. The claim is stale rather than invented, and is contradicted by primary DoD sources. Demonstrates that existence, function, and current status must carry separate grades: this site is simultaneously A and R. Any rubric returning one number for Cheyenne Mountain fails this entry by construction.

calibration_set.name: 33 Thomas Street, Manhattan (AT&T Long Lines Building / TITANPOINTE) — existence and hardening
calibration_set.reasoning: NYC Department of Buildings filings, AT&T's own published engineering and route literature, Warnecke's architectural record, FCC records, and the Snowden material published by The Intercept in November 2016 establish existence, purpose-built hardening, and the international gateway-switch function. Primary sources settle it. Rubric returns 72.11 → B because GEO's mountain-tunnel criteria are inapplicable to a Manhattan tower. Tests the typology-blind weighting defect.

calibration_set.name: The Greenbrier / Project Greek Island, WV — as evidence stood in 1991
calibration_set.expected_grade: C on evidence, but P(exists) HIGH — and it must be published as two numbers
calibration_set.reasoning: The single most important calibration entry. In 1991 this was a fully staffed, 1,100-bed, congressionally mandated COG facility with essentially no documentary trace and a Forsythe Associates cover. Evidence quality was genuinely mediocre; probability of existence was very high given persistent specific local worker testimony plus a low expected-record prior for the category. Rubric returns 22.91 → E, 'folklore with a trace.' Any correct system must refuse to let the evidence grade wear existence language here.

calibration_set.name: The Greenbrier / Project Greek Island — post-1992
calibration_set.reasoning: POSITIVE CONTROL for grade movement. Ted Gup, Washington Post, 31 May 1992; decommissioning followed; the facility is now publicly toured. Rubric returns 90.46 → A, correctly. The regression test is the PAIR: a correct system must record that the transition was caused by disclosure, not by the arrival of new evidence about the physical world.

calibration_set.name: Presidential Emergency Facility 'Cartwheel', Fort Reno Park, Washington DC
calibration_set.reasoning: Existence and function documented in White House Army Signal Agency / WHCA records and in the PEF microwave-network documentation, with a direct AT&T cable route to the White House. Internal extent and current condition partly inferred, so B rather than A. Rubric returns 53.11 → D, 'weak inference,' because the GEO axis finds nothing to reward in a city park and CONTAM penalizes the fact that one careful compiler did the collation. Tests both the typology and the scholarship-vs-rumor CONTAM defects.

calibration_set.name: Iron Mountain / Boyers, PA — OPM Retirement Operations Center
calibration_set.reasoning: Real, mundane, and fully documented: former US Steel limestone mine (excavated 1902-1952), federal records storage from 1960, OPM occupancy from 1970, ~580,000 rentable sq ft per the GSA's 2015 prospectus, OPM's own published material, and extensive named-source journalism. Existence, function, ownership and depth all rest on primary records. Rubric returns 82.74 → B. A useful mid-difficulty positive control: a boring true entry that the rubric slightly under-grades for the same structural reason as 33 Thomas Street.

calibration_set.name: SubTropolis, Kansas City, MO — as a hardened/COG candidate
calibration_set.reasoning: NEGATIVE CONTROL, the false-positive test. An operating commercial underground business park in a former limestone mine, with no defense function. It satisfies GEO and INF criteria almost perfectly (adits, portals, spoil, anomalous road grade, dedicated substation, an actual rail spur, deep wells, fuel permits) and has clean P1 permit documentation. Rubric returns 67.45 → C, 'reasonable inference.' Any correct system must return the bottom of the scale. This is the entry that proves the rubric needs a null hypothesis and likelihood ratios.

calibration_set.name: Montauk Air Force Station / Camp Hero, NY — existence and radar function
calibration_set.reasoning: POSITIVE CONTROL. Army coastal artillery 1942, USAF radar station 1952-1981, AN/FPS-35 within the SAGE network, NARA unit records, closure and disposal records, EPA files, NY State Parks acquisition, standing physical structure. Rubric returns 84.42 → B — one point short of correct, again from axis-weighting drag rather than from any genuine evidentiary gap.

calibration_set.name: 'The Montauk Project' — underground levels, time and mind-control experiments at Camp Hero
calibration_set.reasoning: NEGATIVE CONTROL, and the sharpest test of claims-vs-sites. Traces entirely to Preston B. Nichols' recovered memories in the 1992 book with Peter Moon; every later appearance descends from it. CONTAM 100, no independent lineage, no documentary support. Rubric returns 43.29 → D, 'suggestive but thin,' because the claim inherits the real base's DOC/GEO/INF/OWN. A correct system must score this proposition on its own evidence and land at F.

calibration_set.name: Dulce Base, Archuleta Mesa, NM
calibration_set.expected_grade: F, with the origin documented and a citogenesis flag
calibration_set.reasoning: POSITIVE CONTROL, low end — and the rubric arguably gets it right, at 17.01 → F, but only if CONTAM is set to 95. Following §1.3's own calibration text ('50 = two or three independent origins'), the three named claimants — Bennewitz c.1979-80, 'Thomas Castello' c.1987, Phil Schneider in the 1990s — yield CONTAM ~55 and the entry rises to 23.49 → E. The correct handling is F plus a documented origin: the AFOSI operation against Bennewitz, in which Richard C. Doty supplied forged material to steer him from classified Kirtland programs. That documentation is evidence AGAINST, and a correct system must be able to represent it as such.

calibration_set.name: Deep Underground Command Center (DUCC), Washington DC
calibration_set.expected_grade: A on 'this program was proposed and cancelled'; R on 'this facility exists'
calibration_set.reasoning: Tests the existence/program split and the missing status band. Proposed 1962-64, 3,000-4,000 ft, Austere and Moderate variants, endorsed by McNamara and Rusk, killed when Congress withheld FY1965 funds and refused reprogramming. Documentation is primary and excellent — JCS memoranda in FRUS 1964-68 vol. X, declassified feasibility studies. Rubric returns 37.24 → E, 'folklore with a trace,' six points above Dulce Base. A proven non-facility with superb documentation must not share a bin with an invention.

calibration_set.name: Mount Weather Emergency Operations Center, VA — existence
calibration_set.reasoning: POSITIVE CONTROL. Federally acknowledged, on the public record since at least the TWA Flight 514 crash of 1 December 1974 (NTSB report is P1 and places a federal facility on the mountain), FEMA budget lines, exact location. Rubric handles this correctly.

calibration_set.name: Mount Weather — the 'underground city': streets, sidewalks, a small lake fed by underground springs, its own mass transit system
calibration_set.expected_grade: D, with a citogenesis flag, inside an A-grade site record
calibration_set.reasoning: The most operationally important entry in the set. Every circulating version descends from Richard Pollock, 'The Mysterious Mountain,' The Progressive, March 1976, resting on Senate subcommittee material plus unnamed off-the-record former officials — a P3 publication built on P5 testimony, the exact laundering pattern §1.3 defines. Because the rubric grades sites rather than claims, this content currently rides inside an A-grade entry with the citogenesis flag having nowhere to attach. A correct system prints A on the site and D-with-flag on this specific assertion, on the same page.

calibration_set.name: 'Denver International Airport conceals a deep underground bunker complex'
calibration_set.reasoning: NEGATIVE CONTROL against inherited mundane truth. DIA genuinely has extensive underground tunnels, an operating inter-concourse train, an abandoned automated baggage system (deactivated 2005, leaving empty tunnels), a dedicated substation, deep wells, and enormous documented excavation. Every one of those facts is true, well documented, and diagnostically worthless — each is near-certain under 'it is a very large modern airport.' The bunker claim itself traces to Alex Christopher and Phil Schneider c.1994-96. An axis system that scores signal presence rather than signal discrimination will float this to D or E; the correct answer is F with the 1990s origin on the record.

recommendations: RESTRUCTURE THE UNIT OF ANALYSIS: grade propositions, not places. A site record becomes a container of independently graded claims — EXISTS / HAD FUNCTION X / HAS CURRENT STATUS Y / HAS FEATURE Z / IS AT LOCATION L — each with its own axis scores, CONTAM, provenance, and grade badge. This single change fixes Camp Hero, Mount Weather's 'underground lake', Cheyenne Mountain's stale NORAD status, and the citogenesis flag having nowhere to live. It is a schema decision and must be made before the Postgres design in W3 is locked, because retrofitting claim-level grading onto a site-level table is a migration, not an addition.

GIVE EVIDENCE A SIGN. Every source carries direction (+supports / −undercuts) and magnitude against a named proposition. Add grade band R (REFUTED — affirmatively shown mundane or fabricated, refuting source cited) below F (NO EVIDENCE). F and R are opposite epistemic states and the current scale collapses them, which is why a documented AFOSI disinformation operation reads as DOC credit for Dulce and why a provably commercial cave publishes as C.

PUBLISH TWO NUMBERS, NOT ONE: Q(EVIDENCE) — quality of record, honestly labeled — and P(EXISTS) — probability of existence, informed by an EXPECTED-RECORD prior per era/typology/agency. Where the prior says no public record would be expected, a documentary void must not drag P(EXISTS). Rewrite all six grade band descriptions so they name evidence states and never assert existence. The Greenbrier-in-1991 entry is the regression test: no correct system publishes 'folklore' for an operating congressional relocation site.

REPLACE PRESENCE-SCORING WITH LIKELIHOOD RATIOS AGAINST A NAMED NULL. Every candidate above D must carry an explicitly named-and-rejected mundane alternative ('commercial limestone mine', 'municipal water infrastructure', 'telecom hut'). Signals the null explains equally well score ~0. This is REFUTER's proper numeric hook and it is the only thing that keeps the register from filling with C-grade quarries.

MAKE WEIGHTS TYPOLOGY-CONDITIONAL AND AXES DROPPABLE. Define per-typology weight vectors (buried-rural, urban-hardened, in-building, silo, relay/comms, archive) with typology-specific GEO criteria. An inapplicable axis is renormalized out, never scored zero. Without this, no urban or above-ground hardened facility can reach A regardless of documentation — 33 Thomas Street cannot clear B even with generous scoring.

ADD A DOCUMENTARY SUFFICIENCY OVERRIDE. A P1 source that names the facility, its location, and its function, and is judged authentic, sets a grade FLOOR of B on the existence proposition irrespective of the other five axes. Convergence raises above the floor; its absence must not pull below it. Currently a single conclusive primary document computes to exactly 28.00 → E, which contradicts the rubric's own prose definition of grade A.

COLLAPSE COR AND CONTAM INTO ONE INDEPENDENCE TERM APPLIED ONCE, and rewrite the CONTAM calibration so origins must be CAUSALLY independent rather than merely distinct persons — apply the test 'would this source have produced this claim if the prior source had never existed?'. Compute the lineage graph over ORIGINAL WITNESSES, not over publications, so a transparent compiler citing forty primary documents is not penalized as one rumor lineage. As written, independence carries more score-swing (~40 points) than the entire DOC axis (28 points).

EXTEND THE FIREWALL TO EVERY AXIS, with per-axis caps keyed to the best supporting tier. TEST needs an identity gate — an account is 'named' only if the person is independently confirmed to exist and to have been positioned to know, which excludes 'Thomas Castello' while admitting Greenbrier's construction workers. Score the tier of the INFERENCE, not the artifact: imagery is P2, but 'this imagery shows a blast portal' inherits the tier of whoever asserted it.

TAG EVERY SOURCE WITH SCOPE — class-level or instance-level — and gate DOC accordingly. Class-level evidence feeds a regional PRIOR; only site-identifying evidence feeds instance DOC. Enforce at write time: any source cited by more than one candidate must be marked class-level, or entity resolution is wrong. Otherwise one PEF-program document certifies eight to ten candidate pins at full strength, several of them false.

ADD PROPOSED / STUDIED / CANCELLED / NEVER-BUILT to the Status taxonomy. DUCC is one of the best-documented COG proposals in the American record and currently lands at E, six points above Dulce Base, because the taxonomy's nearest option is 'alleged-only' — which is its epistemic opposite.

GATE MAP RENDERING ON LOCATION PRECISION, not just filtering by it. Anything below 'approximate' renders as a region polygon or county centroid with visible uncertainty, never a point. Grade LOCATION as its own proposition and show both badges in the popup; a candidate can legitimately be A on existence and F on location. A precise pin derived from imprecise evidence is the register manufacturing exactly the kind of durable false fact it exists to dismantle.

ADD PER-AXIS APPLICABILITY/SURVIVAL FLAGS: 'searched, found nothing' / 'record class destroyed' / 'record class never existed for this category' / 'not yet searched'. Only the first is negative evidence. The 12 July 1973 NPRC fire destroyed 16-18 million personnel files — ~80% of Army discharges 1912-1960 and ~75% of USAF 1947-1964, with no duplicates or index — and the TEST axis reads that absence as weak evidence about the facility. Publish the sampling-bias statement on the methodology page: NEPA/EIS availability and FCC registration ANTI-correlate with the sensitivity the register is trying to detect.

ANNOTATE EVERY GRADE TRANSITION WITH ITS CAUSE from a controlled vocabulary (new-disclosure / new-search / re-analysis / refutation / status-change) and render disclosure-driven movement visually distinct from evidence-driven movement. Greenbrier moved E→A on one day in 1992 with no physical change; an unlabeled confidence chart tells the reader the world changed when only the publication record did.

REPLACE REFUTER's blanket 'defaults to refuted under uncertainty' with a typology-conditional prior — default-refute for high-base-rate mundane categories, default-open where the base rate of concealment is known to be high. A uniform refute-by-default prior in a domain where non-disclosure is the norm systematically under-registers the contemporary classified facilities that are the register's whole reason for existing.

RUN THE 15-ENTRY CALIBRATION SET AS A CI REGRESSION TEST before ratifying any revision, and require it to reproduce the expected grades within one band. The pairs are load-bearing: Cheyenne Mountain (site A / status-claim R), Camp Hero (site A / Montauk-claim F), Mount Weather (site A / underground-city D-flagged), and Greenbrier (1991 vs 1993). Any rubric that returns one number per site fails four of those pairs by construction, which is the fastest available proof that the restructuring is necessary rather than optional.
